title: Peña Nieto Filmed Next to Controversial Israeli Contractor
author: Mariana Álvarez Torres
content:
_This article by[Mariana Álvarez
Torres](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/mariana-alvarez-torres) originally
appeared in the [August 30, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4862288/pena-asiste-a-boda-en-italia-y-
lo-graban-junto-a-polemico-contratista-israeli-video/), an independent Mexican
news outlet._

**Mexico City, August 30 (SinEmbargo)**.— Former president **Enrique Peña
Nieto** (EPN) was captured on **video** during the wedding of Israeli singer
Omer Adam, held in Portofino, Italy, seated next to Israeli businessman
**Avishai Neriah** , accused by a media outlet in that country of having
participated in the delivery of **25 million dollars** to the PRI member to
favor contracts within the Mexican government, among them the purchase of the
Pegasus spying system.

The material was recorded during the performance of Hasidic singer Motty
Steinmetz, who took part in the celebration. In it, the former official —also
a lawyer— appears among the guests wearing a **kippah** , traditionally used
by Jewish men.

The event comes a little more than a year after the newspaper The Marker
revealed a series of documents about a dispute between Neriah and businessman
Uri Emmanuel Ansbacher, in which both reportedly acknowledged a "joint
investment" related to a high-ranking figure in the Mexican government. The
outlet identified that person as Enrique Peña Nieto.

According to the investigation, the documents did not specify how the 25
million dollars were used. However, a source cited by the Israeli outlet
maintained that a significant portion of the money was reportedly allocated to
political expenses, possibly related to the 2012 presidential campaign.

The report also indicated that Neriah was the one who had direct access to
Peña Nieto, while both businessmen reportedly used their ties to Mexican
officials to obtain contracts during the PRI six-year term. Among the deals
mentioned was the sale of the Pegasus spying system.

During the administration of Enrique Peña Nieto, between 2012 and 2018,
various Mexican agencies acquired Pegasus, a program developed by the Israeli
company NSO Group to infiltrate cell phones and obtain information from their
users.

That technology was acquired under the argument of using it against organized
crime, but journalistic investigations and those of civil organizations
documented that the phones of journalists, activists, and politicians were
selected as possible espionage targets.

After the report was published, the former PRI president rejected the
accusations and described the information about the alleged payments as
"totally false." He also asserted that he never intervened in the awarding of
contracts and denied knowing the businessmen named.

The Attorney General's Office (FGR) subsequently opened an investigation to
clarify the accusations and requested information from the Israeli authorities
about the content of the report, as well as the arbitration documents.

As of that moment, the Mexican institution stated that it did not have
sufficient evidence to corroborate the accusations.
